critical.issue: doc_type enum in app/config.py:DocumentType still contains ONLY EHS values (sop, incident_report, risk_assessment, regulatory, training, permit, policy, msds, general). The GIS spec asked for doc_type 'book' but 'book' is NOT in the enum. RESULT: if any client sends doc_type='book' (or any non-enum value), the document IS still inserted into Mongo with raw 'book' string (validation happens AFTER insert), then DocumentOut response-model validation fails with 500. The frontend upload form currently sends 'general' for its 'Book / Reference' option so the UI is safe, BUT (a) any external API caller passing 'book' (as the user-facing PRD literally calls out) will poison the DB with an undeserialisable doc, and (b) once 1 poisoned doc exists, GET /api/documents returns 500 forever (Pydantic enum validation in _doc_to_out) which I reproduced — the Documents admin page was broken until I manually deleted the row from Mongo. Fix: add BOOK='book' to DocumentType enum (and/or REJECT invalid doc_type with 400 BEFORE inserting the Mongo row; never insert without validating the enum first).

critical_code_review_comments: doc_type ingestion path inserts FIRST, validates SECOND — a write-before-validate anti-pattern. The DocumentType enum should be enforced at the FastAPI Form() boundary (use the enum class directly as the type hint, not a `str`) so FastAPI rejects unknown values with 422 before any DB write.

/app/backend/app/routes/document_routes.py line 66 (_doc_to_out) re-validates the stored doc against DocumentOut on every list call — a single poisoned row 500s the entire list endpoint indefinitely. Defensive fix: try/except around DocumentOut(**doc) and skip+log invalid rows so the list endpoint stays functional even with legacy data.

rca of the issue: The DocumentType enum was never updated when the EHS→GIS rebrand happened. The upload route accepts doc_type as a plain `str` Form field (document_routes.py:141 — `doc_type: str = Form(DocumentType.GENERAL.value)`), passes the raw string straight into Mongo at line 235, and only later constructs DocumentOut(**doc) where Pydantic enforces the enum and 500s. Because the Mongo insert succeeded, the row persists with the invalid 'book' value, and EVERY subsequent GET /api/documents call calls _doc_to_out on that row → 500 forever (full Documents admin page broken). Reproduction: curl POST /api/documents/upload with multipart doc_type=book → response 500, doc visible in MongoDB ehs_rag.documents, then GET /api/documents returns 500. Mitigation already applied manually for now: db.documents.delete_many({doc_type:'book'}). Permanent fix: change Form signature to `doc_type: DocumentType = Form(DocumentType.GENERAL)` AND add BOOK='book' to the enum, OR add an explicit `if doc_type not in {t.value for t in DocumentType}: raise HTTPException(400, ...)` before the insert. Plus, add try/except around DocumentOut(**doc) in _doc_to_out so legacy/poisoned rows can't take down the whole list endpoint.
